scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

interpretation_history.interpretation: Disputed bills appear for both estimated and actual read types, with actual reads having higher dispute counts. This suggests the dispute increase is not limited to estimation problems; factors affecting actual reads (meter reading, billing processing) also play a role.
No tariff change records were found, indicating that tariff changes are not a source of the recent billing dispute increase.
Route completion for August‑September 2026 is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating that manual field read collection is underperforming and may be contributing to billing disputes.
Dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, showing a clear surge starting in August.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < 3 days SLA) with 2,440 tickets, indicating response speed is not the cause of the dispute surge.

U-U1.question: Whether improving field route completion alone will reduce dispute volume to baseline, or if other factors (AMI read errors, billing rule changes) also contribute.
U-U1.resolution_path: Collect AMI read error rates and billing rule change logs before and after route‑completion improvements to isolate their impact on disputes.

U-U2.question: Accuracy of the claimed staff shortage (three readers missing since July) and its exact quantitative impact on route completion.

problem_definition.root_problem: Insufficient field meter reading capacity due to staff shortage causes route completion below target, leading to missed or incorrect manual reads, increased reliance on estimated bills, and a rise in billing dispute tickets.

trace.summary: Insufficient field meter reading capacity due to staff shortage causes route completion below target, leading to missed or incorrect manual reads, increased reliance on estimated bills, and a rise in billing dispute tickets.

To investigate and mitigate potential AMI read errors and billing rule changes (unknown U-U1) that may remain after field staffing and route optimizations, ensuring dispute volume returns to baseline.

structural_remedies.description: Contract three additional meter readers to eliminate the staff shortage and restore field route completion to target.
structural_remedies.rationale: Staffing increase does not require a protected action; can be initiated within remaining 225 minutes as a planning/commitment step.; residual gap: If AMI read errors or billing rule changes also contribute to disputes, those factors would remain unaddressed by staffing alone. Evidence: E-07, E-03, E-01, U-U1.

structural_remedies.description: Redesign field route sequencing and workload balancing to improve completion rate without adding staff, subject to Field Operations Manager confirmation.
structural_remedies.rationale: Route optimization can be performed in the remaining time; changes to dispatch require runtime confirmation (K-DISPATCH) which can be obtained from SH-FIELD.; residual gap: Staff shortage still caps maximum achievable completion; any residual gap due to missing reads persists. Evidence: E-03, E-07, E-01.

structural_remedies.description: Deploy automated read‑quality validation rules in the billing import pipeline to catch missing or incorrect reads before bill generation, reducing reliance on estimates.
structural_remedies.rationale: Rule changes are configuration updates; they do not involve protected bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) and can be enacted within the remaining time.; residual gap: Does not prevent missing reads from occurring; only mitigates their impact. Residual dispute volume may remain if read errors persist. Evidence: E-01, E-02, U-U1.
